about.title: Monte Sereno Product Liability Claims
about.longDescription: Monte Sereno is a small, tightly-knit Santa Clara County community, but its residents use the same consumer products, vehicles, tools, and appliances found everywhere else — and defects don't discriminate by zip code. Whether the injury happened along Saratoga Los Gatos Road, in a home near La Rinconada Drive, or from a product bought and used locally, California law gives injured people a meaningful path forward. Many product liability claims here rely on strict liability, meaning the focus is on whether the product itself was unreasonably dangerous, not on proving a manufacturer was careless. That distinction matters because it can simplify what an injured person must show. LawProactive doesn't practice law — we connect Monte Sereno residents, free of charge, with an independent attorney experienced in these claims, so you can understand your options without added pressure or upfront cost.

whyChoose.title: What Matters in a California Product Liability Case

items.title: Strict Liability Can Ease the Burden
items.desc: California often allows claims based on strict liability, meaning the injured person generally needs to show the product was defective and caused harm, not that the manufacturer was negligent.

items.title: Multiple Parties May Share Responsibility
items.desc: Manufacturers, distributors, and retailers can all potentially be held liable, which may widen the paths available for pursuing a claim.

items.title: The Product Itself Is Evidence
items.desc: Preserving the defective product exactly as it was at the time of injury can be critical, since it often becomes the centerpiece of showing what went wrong.

items.question: Do I need to prove the manufacturer was careless?
items.answer: Not necessarily. California product liability claims often proceed under strict liability, which generally focuses on whether the product had a defect that caused injury rather than on the manufacturer's conduct. An independent attorney can look at your specific situation and explain which legal theory may apply.

items.question: I live in Monte Sereno — does it matter where the injury happened?
items.answer: What matters most is that the injury occurred and a defective product was involved, whether that was near Winchester Boulevard, Rt 9, or inside your own home. Monte Sereno's small size means local crash and injury numbers are modest, but product defect claims aren't tied to traffic patterns — they follow the product wherever it's used.

items.question: What should I do with the product that caused my injury?
items.answer: Try to keep it in the same condition it was in when the injury happened, including any packaging, parts, or instructions. This preservation can be important evidence later. Avoid repairing or discarding it until you've spoken with an attorney.
